outcome.technical: Edited only PLUGIN-BUILD-GUIDE.md, rewriting two paragraphs from HEAD's code. (1) The deadline paragraph under stamp-verification.py red now says: cost-table figures are slot-seconds; sweep_wall reads one run's wall time as the busiest slot of the sweep's costliest-first schedule (schedule_wall) over sweep_jobs' workers; proof_need is that wall time for each run PROOF_RUNS names; sized_deadline sets TIMEOUT_PER_COST times the need when that exceeds DEFAULT_TIMEOUT, capped at MAX_TIMEOUT; sweep_budget holds the fix run's wall time back, never more than half the deadline; fit_problem refuses before any run, --timeout included and before the throwaway is built, with a basis naming the need, per-run wall time, how it was read and the deadline; start_problem refuses any run started short (the baseline's check also counts the task run); a command with unmeasured wall time is checked by neither. Read from stamp-verification.py: sweep_wall, schedule_wall, sweep_jobs, proof_need, fit_problem, start_problem, sized_deadline, sweep_budget, and the call sites in red near the fit_problem/start_problem calls. (2) The _proc_group section now names drain_to_eof (whether the read reached the pipe's EOF within GRACE_SECONDS) and adds a paragraph on stop_and_drain: tear down, then drain, confirmed only when the kill is confirmed, the drain reached EOF and the root exited; callers run-test-gate._shell (which passes its own _tear_down/_drain_to_eof aliases), stamp-verification._run_in and drive-phase.run_lint_probe, on timeout and interrupt. The task text says every timed-out teardown goes through stop_and_drain, and the code does not bear that out: derive-phase-gate._spawn still calls tear_down then drain on a timeout, and run-agent-session.run_session calls tear_down on an interrupt, and neither records confirmation. The guide states this as it is, and I left both files alone because they are outside my scope. Checks: _deps.doc_prose_numbers(doc_paths=[PLUGIN-BUILD-GUIDE.md]) returned 0 findings (exit 0). The same lint on a scratch copy with a planted 'its 17 cases' line returned 1 finding, so it does scan this file. Grepping the added lines for F/P/BUG ids returned no hits (grep exit 1). Gates: nothing of my own to run (runsGate own-tests, no tests.add); I did not run the task gate (tools/sweep-selftests.py tests/test__deps.py tests/test__output_lints.py), and the orchestrator's recorded run is the evidence. Dependants, all still correct: tests/test__affected_tests.py reads only the guide line starting '_affected_tests.py ', which is unchanged; tests/test__deps.py gp1/gp2 check the guide's path, and map_drift reads tree/map fences, where I added none; tests/test__doctor_trail.py rh11 slices the paragraph starting '**It grades each copy's own age', which is unchanged; tests/test__help.py mentions the guide's map fence only in prose, unchanged; plugins/audit/scripts/status/_doctor_hygiene.py and the two evals case.yaml files mention the guide in comments about tree lines and sections, where I added none; .claude/skills/before-you-claim/evals/evals.json quotes an old guide line as an eval prompt and does not read the file. Other files that were modified before I started (docs/audit/audit-plan.json, P149.json, journal) are the orchestrator's, not mine.
